name: Non-acquired Combined Pituitary Hormone Deficiencies Without Extrapituitary Malformations
aliases: Isolated Combined Hypopituitarism Without Extracranial Anomalies

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Consensus Diagnostic Criteria for Combined Pituitary Hormone Deficiency

criteria.description: Deficiency of two or more anterior pituitary hormones confirmed by biochemical testing
MRI evidence of pituitary hypoplasia or stalk abnormalities without extrapituitary malformations
Exclusion of acquired causes such as tumors, trauma, infection, or radiation
Presence of clinical signs consistent with hormone deficiencies (e.g., growth failure, hypothyroidism, adrenal insufficiency)

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Biochemical confirmation of deficiency in at least two anterior pituitary hormones plus MRI evidence of pituitary abnormalities without extrapituitary malformations, and exclusion of acquired causes.
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Genetic testing may support diagnosis but is not mandatory.

laboratory: Low serum IGF-1 and IGFBP-3 indicating growth hormone deficiency
Low free T4 with low or normal TSH indicating central hypothyroidism
Low morning cortisol and low ACTH indicating secondary adrenal insufficiency
Low LH and FSH with low sex steroids indicating hypogonadotropic hypogonadism
imaging: MRI showing hypoplastic or absent anterior pituitary gland
Normal hypothalamus and absence of extrapituitary malformations
genetic: Mutations in PROP1, POU1F1, HESX1, or other pituitary transcription factor genes (when identified)
other: Normal cranial anatomy excluding extrapituitary malformations
Normal or mildly delayed bone age

distinguishingFeatures: History of trauma, infection, tumor, or radiation
Presence of extrapituitary lesions on imaging
Deficiency limited to growth hormone only
Normal levels of other pituitary hormones
Midline brain abnormalities such as absence of septum pellucidum

redFlags: Failure to thrive with multiple pituitary hormone deficiencies
Sudden adrenal crisis symptoms (hypotension, vomiting, lethargy)
